Ok, yeah I see how this isn't good enough.

What if I made the loop definition like this?

> For each node of select's descendants except the descendants which are select elements and their subtrees in tree order:

I looked around for other spec text which has this pattern of doing a tree traversal which skips certain subtrees, and I found this for option elements which skips over script elements:

> The text IDL attribute, on getting, must return the result of [stripping and collapsing ASCII whitespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#strip-and-collapse-ascii-whitespace) from the concatenation of [data](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-cd-data) of all the [Text](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#interface-text) node descendants of the [option](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-option-element) element, in [tree order](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-tree-order), excluding any that are descendants of descendants of the [option](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-elements.html#the-option-element) element that are themselves [script](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#the-script-element) or [SVG script](https://svgwg.org/svg2-draft/interact.html#ScriptElement) elements.

body:
The rationale for this is that if the option is inside a select element which is also inside another select element and a subtree was disconnected between the two selects, then we shouldn't update any of the selects. Here's an example:
```html
<select id=s1>
  <!-- Let's pretend that the parser lets us nest <select>s -->
  <select id=s2>
    <option>option</option>
  </select>
</select>
<script>
  s2.remove();
</script>
```
The idea is that the option is associated with s2, not s1, so we shouldn't try to update s2 or s1 since there are no changes which affect the association of selects and their options.

Since these steps run after the DOM has been updated to do the disconnection, then s1 should no longer be an ancestor of the option, but s2 will be.

In chromium there is more manual bookkeeping to associate options and selects so it's important there that we don't try to update any selects in this case, but I suppose that in this spec we could just run the "selectedness setting algorithm" anyway and it shouldn't actually have any side effects, so I suppose that we could just remove this line and it would be ok.

Does this make sense? Given the last paragraph do you think we should remove this line?

I'm not sure we need to drop `input` elements when fragment parsing with the context element being `select`. It was already possible to get `input` elements in `select` with `option.innerHTML = '<input>'`: https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/13591

You can also insert a `select` element (whose start tag will be parsed as an end tag in a reparse): https://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/saved/13592

Changes such as the ones below would be more effective at preventing mXSS, since you need to exploit a situation where something is considered "text" (attribute value or RAWTEXT element) in one context but markup in another context.

- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6235
- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10879
- https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9426

I agree with @zcorpan here. I don't believe this change introduces any new mXSS technique (even if some *mutations* exist).

I would even go as far as saying that this change could be security-positive. Internally at Google we're aware of HTML sanitizer bypass existing because of the fact that the sanitizer wasn't aware of the special parsing rules for `<select>` (so the discrepancy could be exploited). When this change is in effect, the bypass doesn't work anymore because `<select>` is now parsed  as any other tag.

body:
The issue is that there are a lot of cases where `innerHTML` can be used to create a DOM that is mutated upon serialize-parse, and we likely can't start to drop elements without breaking the web. Doing so only for `input` in `select` but not `input` in `option` in `select` or `h2` in `h1` or any foster-parented content in `table`, and so on, doesn't seem like it solves anything. So my conclusion is that we should let `input` be inserted.

Also see https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10310#issuecomment-2304377029
